judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare consideration/reliance preamble; nothing in it carries two reasonable meanings beyond ordinary OCR garbling.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It simply subjects everything to 'all the terms of this policy', which is consistent with the Declarations and the endorsement schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The core insuring clause turns entirely on defined terms ('ultimate net loss', 'retained limit', 'occurrence', 'personal injury') and on the elastic phrase 'to which this policy applies', which litigants routinely read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its scope is heavily rewritten downstream by the Professional Services Excluded endorsement (c082), the Personal Injury Endorsement (c058) and the Aggregate Limits Endorsement (c084), so whether professional liability is covered at all cannot be settled from this clause alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger — an occurrence 'not covered by any underlying coverage ... or any other underlying insurance collectible by the insured' — leaves 'collectible' undefined and is a familiar site of argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the immediately following paragraphs (c008, c009) and with Condition 13 Maintenance of Underlying Insurance (c056), which deems unmaintained underlying cover to remain in force.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A duty to defend 'even if such suit is groundless, false or fraudulent' coupled with a discretionary right to settle 'as it deems expedient' is standard but the two halves pull against each other.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Asbestos Exclusion expressly negates any defence obligation (c081), and c008 removes defence covered by underlying insurance, so the defence duty is fragmented across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow, mechanical bond-premium obligation with an express disclaimer of any duty to furnish bonds; little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the policy addresses bonds, so no conflict is visible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard costs-and-post-judgment-interest wording, capped by reference to the limit of liability; definite in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the 'ultimate net loss' definition (c033), which excludes court costs and interest, but the two are complementary rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reimbursement of reasonable expenses other than loss of earnings, only when incurred at the company's request — a tightly bounded promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c010, which makes supplementary payments additional to ultimate net loss.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and apparently definite, but 'covered by underlying insurance' is doing a lot of work where underlying cover is disputed or exhausted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be harmonised with the Supplementary Payments lead-in (c003) and with c009, which imposes a defence duty once underlying limits are exhausted; the boundary between them is not spelled out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The condition 'immediately in excess of underlying insurance listed on the declarations page without intervening insurance' is a genuine operative qualifier that parties read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts directly with the Retained Limit definition (c034), Loss Payable (c048) and Maintenance of Underlying Insurance (c056), which treat exhaustion and attachment on different premises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out 'except settlement of claims or suits' is compressed and its reach over the preceding four sub-paragraphs is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on the Limit of Liability (c013/c084) by placing some sums outside the limit, but no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prevented by law or otherwise' is open-ended, and the substituted obligation (pay expenses incurred with written consent) is vaguely tied to 'this agreement'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses jurisdictions where the defence obligation cannot be performed, so no conflict is identifiable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear reimbursement obligation keyed to Item 4 of the declarations; the wording itself is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes the company pays within the SIR, which sits awkwardly with Loss Payable (c048) providing that liability does not attach until the underlying limit has been paid, and with the 'greater of' Retained Limit definition (c034).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The aggregate proviso limits only products/completed-operations loss while the Declarations state a general aggregate, leaving the aggregate's reach uncertain on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This paragraph is expressly replaced by the Aggregate Limits Endorsement (c084) and the amounts are again changed by Endorsement No. 4 (c109), so three different texts of the limit sit in the assembled policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Occurrences happening anywhere' is about as definite as a territory clause can be.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Two Policy Territory Amended endorsements (c105, c113) purport to amend territory provisions of a 'Hospital Professional Liability coverage part' that is not part of this umbrella form, leaving the relationship unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional workers'/unemployment compensation exclusion; the trailing 'or similar law' is a modest catch-all but a very familiar one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy grants employers-liability-type cover except the underlying schedule, which is consistent with excess treatment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate nuclear energy liability exclusion drawn from a standard industry form with its own definitions supplied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision touches nuclear risk; irrelevant to a paediatric hospital programme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard nuclear-material exclusion; the internal cross-reference to 'exclusion (5)' is garbled but the substance is the familiar form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is defined by c018 and does not bear on any other operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional appendix keyed to the Atomic Energy Act; definite by statutory incorporation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Serves only exclusions (b) and (c); no other provision depends on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The excerpt runs the loss-of-use exclusion together with the definitions section, but the substantive carve-back for 'sudden and accidental physical injury' is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the Property Damage definition (c036), which itself covers loss of use of undamaged property, creating a grant/exclusion interface.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any other organization coming under the named insured's control of which it assumes active management' uses two vague tests — 'control' and 'active management' — whose boundary is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Additional Named Insureds endorsement (c085) says 'no automatic coverage for entities newly acquired' and Endorsements 6-8 (c115, c117, c120) add entities one by one, which pulls against automatic status under this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Heavily degraded text of a standard 'insured' clause extending to executive officers, directors and stockholders acting within the scope of their duties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Directors and Officers exclusion (c076) and its carve-out (c078) qualify exactly this group, so the two must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fragmentary omnibus-automobile clause; substance is standard permissive-user cover.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Automobile definition (c040) and the automobile liability entry in Item 7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The aircraft exclusion is qualified by 'except insofar as coverage is provided in the underlying insurance as scheduled herein', a following-form qualifier whose scope is not spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No aircraft cover appears in the Item 7 schedule, so the exception may be a dead letter; it also has to be read with the Aircraft definition (c039).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The care-custody-or-control limb is qualified 'to the extent the insured is under contract to provide insurance', a condition that is easy to dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Care, Custody & Control Exclusion (c075) covers the same ground far more broadly and without that qualification, so two overlapping exclusions of different width sit in one policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional sistership/recall exclusion; the concepts are well worn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Products hazard definition (c041) and the aggregate proviso in c013/c084.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'But this shall not relate to use of slogans' is an oddly worded exception whose direction (carve-in or carve-out) is not clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Advertising Liability definition (c037) expressly covers infringement of slogan, so the exclusion and definition point in opposite directions on slogans.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard racing/demolition-contest exclusion; concrete and bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses racing activity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'sudden and accidental' carve-back to a pollution exclusion is one of the most contested phrases in liability insurance, and this rendering is truncated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Total Pollution Exclusion (c093-c096) states that it replaces this exclusion, so whether the sudden-and-accidental carve-back survives depends on matching the replaced text, which does not correspond word for word.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A badly degraded omnibus clause covering watercraft, aircraft and contractual additional insureds; the underlying form is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the aircraft exclusion (c023) and the contractual exclusion endorsement (c057), which limits liability assumed under contract.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stray fragment of a sub-paragraph; too little text to name a defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Belongs to the omnibus insured clause and adds nothing that conflicts elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Extending insured status to anyone insured under 'any policy of underlying insurance' subject to all its limitations 'other than the limits' is broad and its interaction with the underlying wording is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts across the carefully enumerated Additional Named Insureds (c085) and Additional Insureds (c088) endorsements, which would be surplusage if this limb operated freely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional on the Named Insured being designated a partnership or joint venture, and the wording is the familiar form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations designate a corporation, so the limb is inapplicable on its face — a dormant rather than conflicting provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Ultimate net loss' excludes 'all loss expenses and legal expenses' yet the closing words ('the company or any underlying insurer so incurred') are syntactically broken, leaving whose expenses are excluded genuinely unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the Supplementary Payments provisions (c006, c010) and the Overlap Endorsement (c106), which promise indemnity for legal expenses that this definition strips out of loss.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Retained limit means the greater of' the scheduled underlying limits plus other collectible insurance, or the SIR where underlying insurance is 'inapplicable' — 'inapplicable' and 'collectible' are both open, and this is the classic attachment-point fight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with Loss Payable (c048), the SIR reimbursement clause (c012), Maintenance of Underlying Insurance (c056) and the endorsement increasing underlying professional limits to $1M/$3M (c121), which move the attachment point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A composite definition mixing bodily injury with offence-type torts; item (5) covers discrimination 'not committed by or on behalf of the insured', a qualifier that is hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Two endorsements strike large parts of it — FF-15 (c058) removes mental injury, shock, false arrest, libel and privacy, and X-20 (c079) removes discrimination — so the operative definition can only be assembled by layering three texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard two-limb property damage definition with a policy-period trigger; well settled wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the Occurrence definition (c038) and the loss-of-use exclusion (c019) without evident contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional advertising liability definition; 'idea misappropriation under an implied contract' is narrow and specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The advertising offence exclusion (c026) contains a slogan qualifier that pulls against limb (2) of this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Accident, including continuous or repeated exposure', 'neither expected nor intended from the standpoint of the insured', and the deeming rule for exposure 'to substantially the same general conditions ... from one location or source' are all classic sites of construction, especially on number of occurrences.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives the each-occurrence and aggregate limits (c013/c084) and the Loss Payable and Retained Limit machinery, so how many occurrences there are changes the whole indemnity calculation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line, concrete definition of aircraft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only by the aircraft exclusion (c023); no tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line, concrete definition of automobile.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the omnibus automobile limb (c022) and Item 7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition opens with 'personal injury and property damage' but then conditions on 'the bodily injury or property damage', a mismatch of defined terms that changes what falls inside the hazard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The products hazard is the trigger for the aggregate limit in c013 and c084, so the mismatch matters to the limit structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard completed-operations hazard definition tied to c043; well-worn wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Feeds the aggregate proviso in c013/c084 consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but mechanical definition with express completion triggers and express carve-outs; internally self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supports c042 and the aggregate limit; no visible conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence pointing to the declarations; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Pay Plan Endorsement (c097-c098) supplies instalments consistent with the declared premium of $29,890.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An inspection right expressly disclaimed as an undertaking; carefully drafted and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision imposes safety duties on the company.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Whenever it appears that an occurrence is likely to involve indemnity' and notice 'as soon as practicable' are elastic standards that generate late-notice litigation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs alongside Condition 13's requirement of notice of exhaustion within 30 days (c056) and the Wisconsin amendatory endorsement's agent-knowledge and prejudice rules (c072, c073), which soften strict compliance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A discretionary appeal right with an express cap; the wording is definite despite OCR damage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Limit of Liability and with the exclusion of costs from ultimate net loss.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not attach until the amount of the underlying limit has been paid by or on behalf of the insured' is the classic exhaustion trigger, and 'by or on behalf of' is contested wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits uneasily with the Retained Limit definition (c034), which permits attachment over a mere SIR where underlying insurance is inapplicable, and with c056, which deems unmaintained underlying policies still in force.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fragment as it survives states only a no-direct-action and no-impleader rule; badly degraded but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement (c070) deletes the 'Action Against Company' condition 'in its entirety' and substitutes text expressly entitling any person or organization to recover, which is the opposite of this fragment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line bankruptcy clause; the concept is settled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is duplicated verbatim inside the Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement (c070), which raises only a redundancy, not a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As rendered the clause runs an assignment restriction into what appears to be a death-of-insured provision ('shall cover the insured's legal ... for the unexpired portion of such period'), leaving the sentence without a coherent subject.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses assignment, so the defect is intrinsic rather than relational.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An excess-over-other-insurance clause with a parenthetical carve-out and a pro-rata contribution proviso; the phrases 'other valid and collectible insurance' and 'stated to be primary, contributing, excess or contingent' are heavily litigated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with the Retained Limit definition (c034), which already counts 'other underlying insurance collectible', and with the Overlap Endorsement (c106) governing inter-insurer disputes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed apportionment waterfall; mechanical rather than ambiguous, though the ordering language is degraded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement (c071) adds a made-whole rule that reorders recovery, which pulls against the waterfall's stated priority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional no-waiver / endorsement-only-change clause; definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement 'CHANGES' provision (c072) says knowledge of an agent is knowledge of the company and shall not void the policy, which directly contradicts this clause's statement that notice to or knowledge of any agent effects no waiver or change.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is badly mangled, with the insured-cancellation sentence broken and a thirty-day company notice stated as '(20)' in figures — a mechanical discrepancy between word and numeral.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Cancellation endorsement (c063-c069) allows cancellation on ten days' notice while Endorsement No. 3 (c092) requires sixty days, so three different notice periods coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A warranty of maintenance whose remedy — the policy applies 'in the same manner as it would have applied had such policies been so maintained' — is a drop-down/deemed-limit formula that parties read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against Loss Payable (c048), which requires actual payment of the underlying limit, and against Retained Limit (c034), which substitutes the SIR when underlying cover is inapplicable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except insofar as coverage is available to the insured in the underlying insurance listed' is grammatically incomplete (listed where?) and the following-form exception's reach is left undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the coverage grant (c002) and interacts with the omnibus insured limb covering persons to whom the named insured is obligated by written contract to provide insurance (c029), which assumes contractual liability cover.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception is keyed to 'the underlying insurance or self insured retention listed in Item 7 of the Declarations', but the self-insured retention is stated in Item 4, not Item 7 — a mis-citation that changes when the endorsement bites.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It strips out most of the Personal Injury definition (c035) while the Cross Suits carve-out (c060) and D&O carve-out (c078) still assume personal injury and professional cover, so the true scope of 'personal injury' has to be assembled across four texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An insured-versus-insured bar reaching claims 'initiated, alleged or caused to be brought about by' a Named Insured, wording broad enough to invite argument about indirect involvement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With the long Named Insured list in c085 and the additions in c115, c117 and c120, the exclusion sweeps across many affiliated entities, and its own carve-outs (c060, c061) qualify it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The conditional opener 'if this policy applies to professional liability' leaves the carve-out contingent on a question the policy does not answer in one place.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Professional Services Excluded endorsement (c082) excludes professional health care services subject to a Patients Compensation Fund carve-out (c083), while the Aggregate Limits Endorsement (c084) assumes a 'professional liability hazard' exists — so whether this carve-out ever operates is genuinely contested.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Inapplicable as respects intrafamily liability coverage in cases of automobile liability' is terse and its operation in a corporate hospital programme is obscure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No intrafamily coverage appears anywhere in the policy, so the sentence has no evident referent in the instrument.
